message.content: [ISSUE #1] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)] Description: The "Java Arguments" input field contains text "-XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled" with insufficient contrast against the dark background. The text color appears to be #CCCCCC (or similar light gray) on a #1E1E1E background, resulting in a contrast ratio of approximately 4.2:1, which is below the required 4.5:1 for normal text. Impact: Users with visual impairments (e.g., low vision, color blindness) will struggle to read the Java arguments, increasing the risk of input errors and configuration mistakes that could prevent the game from launching properly. Fix: Change the input field text color to #FFFFFF (white) or #E0E0E0 (light gray) to achieve a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio. Example CSS: `input[type="text"] { color: #FFFFFF; }` [ISSUE #2] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.1.1 Keyboard] Description: The "Browse" button in the "Custom Minecraft Location" section lacks a visible focus indicator when navigated to via keyboard (Tab key). The button appears to have no border or background change on focus, making it impossible for keyboard-only users to determine which element is currently selected. Impact: Keyboard-dependent users cannot identify the active element, leading to confusion and potential misinteraction (e.g., accidentally clicking the wrong button). Fix: Add a visible focus ring to all interactive elements. Example CSS: `button:focus { outline: 2px solid #4CAF50; outline-offset: 2px; }` [ISSUE #3] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast] Description: The toggle switches for "Hide on Launch" and "In-Game Overlay" have insufficient contrast between the active (green) state and the background. The green color (#4CAF50) on the dark background (#1E1E1E) results in a contrast ratio of approximately 2.8:1, below the required 3:1 for non-text UI components. Impact: Users with low vision may not distinguish the active state of the toggles, leading to uncertainty about whether a setting is enabled or disabled. Fix: Increase the contrast of the active toggle state. Use a brighter green (e.g., #66BB6A) or add a subtle border. Example CSS: `.toggle.active { background-color: #66BB6A; border: 1px solid #4CAF50; }` [ISSUE #4] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.4.7 Focus Visible] Description: The "Fullscreen" label next to the toggle switch lacks a visible focus indicator when the associated toggle is focused. The label text does not change appearance (e.g., no underline or color shift) on focus, making it unclear which element is active. Impact: Users relying on keyboard navigation cannot easily identify the focused element, reducing usability and increasing error risk. Fix: Apply a focus style to the toggle label. Example CSS: `label.toggle-label:focus { outline: 1px dotted #FFFFFF; }` [ISSUE #5] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 5. Error Prevention] Description: The "Custom Minecraft Location" section includes a "Browse" button and a "Default Location" button, but there is no confirmation dialog or warning when changing the game data folder. This is a high-risk action that could lead to data loss or corruption if the user selects an incorrect path. Impact: Users may accidentally select a non-Minecraft folder, causing the game to fail to launch or corrupt save data, with no clear recovery path. Fix: Add a confirmation modal for the "Browse" action. Example: When "Browse" is clicked, show a dialog: "Are you sure you want to change the Minecraft data folder? This may affect your saves and mods. [Cancel] [Confirm]". [ISSUE #6] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Fitts's Law] Description: The "Browse" and "Default Location" buttons in the "Custom Minecraft Location" section are too small (approximately 32px height) and too close together (8px gap), violating Fitts's Law. The target size is insufficient for easy mouse interaction, especially for users with motor impairments. Impact: Users may misclick the buttons, leading to frustration and repeated attempts to interact with the correct control. Fix: Increase button height to 40px and add 12px horizontal spacing between buttons. Example CSS: `button { height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; margin-right: 12px; }` [ISSUE #7] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value] Description: The toggle switches for "Hide on Launch" and "In-Game Overlay" lack ARIA labels, making them inaccessible to screen reader users. The toggles are represented as images or custom elements without semantic meaning. Impact: Screen reader users cannot determine the purpose of the toggles or their current state (on/off). Fix: Add ARIA labels and roles. Example HTML: `` [ISSUE #8] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 8. Aesthetic and Minimalist Design] Description: The "Java & Launch" settings page includes a description ("Executable path, JVM arguments, and game launch defaults") that is redundant with the section title. This adds unnecessary visual noise and clutter. Impact: The redundant text wastes screen space and may confuse users about the purpose of the section. Fix: Remove the descriptive text below the "JAVA & LAUNCH" heading, as the title is self-explanatory. [ISSUE #9] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Law of Proximity] Description: The "Window Size" input fields (1024 and 768) and the "Fullscreen" toggle are not grouped visually, despite being related to the same setting. The toggle is separated by a large gap (24px) from the input fields, breaking the Law of Proximity. Impact: Users may not associate the fullscreen toggle with the window size settings, leading to confusion about how the settings interact. Fix: Move the "Fullscreen" toggle closer to the window size inputs (reduce gap to 8px) and add a subtle divider or grouping container. [ISSUE #10] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus] Description: The "Browse" button has no hover state, making it unclear to users that it is an interactive element. The button appears static and unresponsive on mouse hover. Impact: Users may not realize the button is clickable, reducing discoverability and interaction. Fix: Add a hover state to the "Browse" button. Example CSS: `button:hover { background-color: #45a049; }` [VISUAL HIERARCHY & LAYOUT]: PASS — no issues found. [COLOR & CONTRAST]: Issues found (see #1, #3). [INTERACTIVE FEEDBACK]: Issues found (see #2, #10). [FORM DESIGN]: Issues found (see #1, #7). [NAVIGATION]: PASS — no issues found. [LOADING & EMPTY STATES]: PASS — no issues found. [ERROR HANDLING]: Issues found (see #5). [RESPONSIVENESS]: PASS — no issues found. [ACCESSIBILITY]: Issues found (see #2, #4, #7). [CONSISTENCY]: PASS — no issues found. [PERFORMANCE PERCEPTION]: PASS — no issues found. [MINIMALISM]: Issues found (see #8).
